artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Kill The Wolf" is the fourth studio album by English musician and comedian Matt Berry, originally released in 2013 by Acid Jazz Records. The album blends elements of rock, folk, and psychedelic pop, characterized by its autumnal, gothic atmosphere and darkly whimsical lyrical themes. Berry's songwriting explores nature, rural imagery, and the cycles of life and death, often with a surreal, psychedelic twist. Musically, the album features lush arrangements, atmospheric synths, and guitar work that ranges from pastoral folk to expansive, David Gilmour-inspired solos, particularly on the epic track "Solstice." Berry produced the album himself and performed most of the instruments, resulting in a deeply personal and idiosyncratic sound.

Within Matt Berry's discography, "Kill The Wolf" stands as a pivotal release, marking a shift toward a more mature and cohesive artistic vision following his earlier, more experimental works. The album received generally favorable reviews, earning a Metacritic score of 71/100, and was praised for its eccentric production flourishes and Berry's unique blend of psychedelic folk and progressive rock. Critics noted its mysterious, eccentric character and its ability to balance quirky, childlike imagery with darker, fatalistic undertones. "Kill The Wolf" remains a distinctive entry in the Acid Jazz catalog and a standout in Berry's musical career.
